s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and skin symptoms with a progressive rash
salient_findings: Pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting on the trunk
key_facts: Age of the patient is in the 60s
Initial symptoms include asthenia, anorexia, and cough
Hospitalization occurred six days after symptom onset
Papules were asymptomatic and measured 3- to 6-mm
Papules evolved to a purpuric rash within 48 hours
Nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR tests for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 were negative
Immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses were negative
RT-PCR testing of fixed skin tissue for SARS-CoV-2 was negative
Histologic analysis showed extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis
Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration were present
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis and large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive rash with purpuric evolution and mucocutaneous involvement

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic papules with superficial crusting and rapid progression to purpuric rash

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Papulovesicular eruption with superficial crust and perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including the rapid progression from papules to a purpuric rash and the histologic findings of extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis, are consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis. The negative tests for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 also support this diagnosis, as these conditions can cause similar skin manifestations but were ruled out.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: While similar to toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome typically involves less than 10% of the body surface area and is often associated with mucosal involvement, which was not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is more common in children and is caused by staphylococcal toxins, which were not mentioned in the case. The patient's age and the lack of evidence for staphylococcal infection make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema multiforme is characterized by target lesions and is often associated with herpes simplex or other infections, which were ruled out by negative tests. The patient's skin manifestations and histologic findings are not consistent with erythema multiforme.

rejected.label: Vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient's histologic analysis showed early-stage vasculitic alterations, the primary diagnosis of toxic epidermal necrolysis better explains the patient's symptoms and skin manifestations. Vasculitis may be a secondary or contributing factor, but it is not the primary diagnosis.
